title: Chapter 1867: Mansion Water And Inferior Water (I)
content:
Chapter 1867: Mansion Water And Inferior Water (I)

By the time Li Ximing saw the two Daoist Masters off, night had fallen. Light and shadow mingled among the island's buildings, with figures moving to and fro.

Naturally, the Li Family had not invited the two Daoist Masters into Zhen Tao Residence. Only at this moment did Li Ximing descend on the wind and enter the deep-blue cave dwelling, where black and white intertwined. At its center, the [Wall-Sinking Water] had turned pure white, clearly ready to be collected.

Yehui took an entire pool of [Wall-Sinking Water], but it yields only two portions when used here. Once I collect this second portion, I'll have two [Under-Neck Feathers] in hand, but the supply will run dry again.

Grandfather's treatment cost one [Late-Blooming Golden Branch] and one [Under-Neck Feather]... This more or less offsets that expense.

He looked up to see Liu Changdie leading someone inside. Spotting him, Liu Changdie smiled. "Fellow Daoist Zhaojing! Come meet someone!"

Li Ximing looked over. The Daoist Master following Liu Changdie stood only as tall as his shoulder. Her long hair was tied up, and her features were delicate and gentle, though her eyes held a deep, somber hue. The sound of bubbling spring water seemed to accompany her steps.

Before he could speak, the woman bowed and smiled. "Baoxiang of Mount Bojun greets you, senior!"

Neither of the two earlier Daoist Masters had entered this place, yet Liu Changdie had openly brought Daoist Master Baoxiang inside. Clearly, he trusted her a great deal!

Li Ximing immediately warmed to her. Seeing how young she looked, he courteously returned her greeting and was about to address her as a peer when Liu Changdie smiled. "This child only reached the Purple Mansion Realm two years ago. She's a junior of a friend of mine, so she ought to address you as a senior!"

When he heard the name Mount Bojun, Li Ximing realized that Liu Changdie had taken the Western Sea venture to heart and contacted her in advance.

Inwardly grateful, he smiled. "The younger generation certainly has no shortage of talent!"

Baoxiang repeatedly demurred, but Liu Changdie's expression grew serious. "She cultivates [Pit Water] through the Heavenborn Devil Dao, supported by Diverse Mansion. Her divine ability is [Holding the Ridge]. She comes from a distinguished lineage herself!"

He paused before adding, "For the Western Sea venture... I've asked her to guide you there."

Li Ximing thanked him, then said, "I would still appreciate your guidance, senior."

Liu Changdie sat down with them. Pouring tea, he began quietly, "The Western Sea... is more than a single sea. It would be more fitting to call it the Western Seas. Traveling northwest from the plateau, past Dayuan, you come to an inland sea called the [Northern High Thunderflight Sea], as large as the land of Shu. Beyond several mountains lies another sea of comparable size, called the [Great Sea]. Dashi lies between the two.

"Only after crossing the [Great Sea] do you reach the heart of the Western Seas. It is called the [Sea Within the Mansion], larger than Jiangnan and comparable to the Scarlet Pristine Sea. It can also simply be called the [Western Sea]!"

Liu Changdie smiled. "This Western Sea is particularly unusual. Encircled by mountains and islands, it resembles an enormous lake, yet its water is salty. Its peculiar geography embodies the nature of lakes and marshes, earning it [Mansion Water]'s favor. It was the earliest site of Dao attainment through Mansion Water, and a place that embodies its symbolism!"

Li Ximing had visited Dashi before. Its peoples' fondness for head coverings had left a deep impression on him, but he had only traveled between the [Northern High Thunderflight Sea] and the [Great Sea], never venturing farther west. He had long heard of the connection between the Western Sea and Mansion Water, but only now understood its origins.

He could not help exclaiming, "No wonder Mansion Water favors it. An entire sea lies inland!"

It was hardly the only such place. Li Ximing immediately thought of the familiar Lake Xian in Jiangnan. Said to have been left behind by a battle between mighty cultivators, it resembled a lake but connected to the sea, likewise embodying Mansion Water's symbolism. That was why Li Wushao, who cultivated Mansion Water, had been so reluctant to leave it, until his elder relative Li Yuanjiao had brought him home.

"Even the old Moongaze Marsh was called a sacred land of Mansion Water. A lake as vast as a sea... how much more favor must it receive!"

Liu Changdie nodded slightly. Having listened for a while, Baoxiang said thoughtfully, "Mansion Water once had two branches, usually regarded as the immortal and devil branches. One was based on an ancient mountain near the [Northern High Thunderflight Sea]. It focused on the powers of Inferior Water's offshoot, and was what the Xia people traditionally understood as [Inferior Water]. The other was based in what is now the Western Sea and focused on Mansion Water's vastness.

"In those days, the Western Sea was far more formidable than it is now, with abundant spiritual energy. Since Mansion Water's vastness predominated, Inferior Water's mystics were not especially pronounced and the former enjoyed great prosperity. After all, it was far from the mainland and the attention of mighty cultivators.

“Its people were not Xia, either, and observed far fewer strictures concerning Dao lineages and their doctrines. It was a sacred land for devil cultivators. There was even a great nation built around the sea, called Great Qin. It, too, unleashed its share of bloodshed...

"Later, some upheaval or dispute arose involving the dragons. After that, the ancient immortal mountain vanished, and the Western Sea's connection to Mansion Water steadily weakened. Worse, Inferior Water's abilities also escaped control, wreaking destruction unchecked. The waters became uniform, unchanging, and difficult to fly across, which gradually led to the region’s decline year after year."

She seemed deeply familiar with these matters and explained them clearly. Li Ximing replied thoughtfully, "So the distinction between Mansion Water and Inferior Water... dates back that far."

The woman smiled. "Indeed... Cultivators of the Western Sea don't even know what Inferior Water is. Only you mainland cultivators of the higher realms call it that."

The Li Family had first heard the name Inferior Water long ago, from Yang Xiao'er. A casual remark by that imperial descendant, who had ties to the Underworld's judiciary, had shaped the family's initial understanding of Inferior Water.

But Li Ximing also keenly recalled something.

Why can Mansion Water's Dao not be attained? Alas, the Yu

[1] seized the abyss; the Profound Turtle lost its vastness; and its nature has been difficult to reconcile ever since!

Those were the words recorded by the former master of Zhen Tao Residence! Clearly, the immense Western Sea could very well correspond to Mansion Water's [Vastness]!

Mansion Water had most likely been severed from [Vastness], narrowing its original authority until it was confined entirely to lakes and marshes. That would explain why the Western Sea had lost its connection to Mansion Water!

That upheaval she mentioned... was probably the seizure of the abyss that gave Pit Water [Boundless Ocean]!

His heart grew a little heavy. With this deeper understanding of Mansion Water, he remained silent for a long while. His silence prompted the woman to weigh her words.

She glanced at Liu Changdie and said, "I hear you are interested in the Western Sea's affairs and [Wall-Sinking Water], senior... I have a suggestion or two..."

Li Ximing's eyes brightened, and he smiled. "Please, go ahead!"

Daoist Master Baoxiang said, "[Wall-Sinking Water] may not be particularly precious, but gathering a large quantity is no easy task. If you need it, it would be best to entrust the matter to [Mercury Circulation Terrace]... We can discuss the details, but as for the situation..."

Liu Changdie, who had listened silently until now, set down his cup and offered a reminder. "There is a [Temple of Gained Affection] on [Lesser Broadsky Mountain], presided over by Abbot Shehu. He and I have an old grievance, and the spirit water in his possession happens to suit Daoist Master Zhaojing's needs. That is the matter he has come to settle."

Li Ximing committed this to memory, but Baoxiang's delicate brows drew together. "I understand... But Abbot Shehu is a close friend of the [Western Mansion Origin Grotto Gate]. I hope you will both consider this carefully and proceed with caution."

Baoxiang was no fool. She had already caught the killing intent in Liu Changdie's words. This was a delicate matter. If anything went wrong, her involvement might drag her into trouble as well. She was only willing to help because Liu Changdie had asked. Had it been anyone else, she would have wanted no part in it.

Liu Changdie turned to meet Li Ximing's gaze and transmitted his voice,

I'll leave the arrangements to you, Zhaojing. My grievance with Shehu isn't particularly deep, but disposing of him would be no great matter. You must simply strike swiftly and decisively. If it drags on, someone will certainly come to his rescue...

His cultivation isn't particularly high, though he does have two divine abilities. He cultivates [Orthodox Wood]. Are you confident?

Li Ximing had no shortage of people he could call upon. With Yan Dushui and Guo Nanwu, two seemingly unrelated figures, assisting from the sidelines, there were countless ways to arrange matters. Add several spirit treasures and Li Zhouwei's intervention, and Shehu would not escape even if he sprouted wings.

He simply replied,

Rest assured!

Having given his assurance, Li Ximing looked up with a smile and said, "I'll trouble your lineage to make the arrangements. I will act when the opportunity arises. If matters truly cannot be reconciled, someone will deal with him."

Daoist Master Baoxiang considered this silently for a moment, then nodded. "I understand."

1. 蜮 (yù) is a mythical water creature said to harm people by spitting sand at them or their shadows. ☜
